item.description:

It includes total cholesterol, blood pressure, blood glucose, BMI, waist circumference height, weight and body mass index measurements. item.title: Incredible Science — Sat Aug 8, 12:30 PM — Downtown Raleigh
item.description:
Join us for an entertaining half hour of science experiments and demonstrations. Day-to-day topics vary but often include physics and chemistry demonstrations on inertia, buoyancy and electromagnetism. Enjoy natural science topics such as the incredible composition of beaver teeth or the amazing design and strength of birds’ eggs. This walk-up program is offered:
Wednesdays — 1:30pm Thursdays — 1:30pm Fridays — 1:30pm Saturdays — 12:30pm, 2pm
Location: Windows on the World on the 3rd floor of the Nature Exploration Center. Designed for ages 7 and up. No registration required.
Source: NC Museum of Natural Sciences

item.title: Science Today: Intro to Bacteria — Sat Aug 8, 1:00 PM — Nature Research Center
item.description:
Today’s Topic Bacteria are the oldest lifeforms on Earth and outnumber us even in our own bodies. Together, we’ll learn more about what they do, where they came from, and how they can affect our health. Today’s Expert Melody Xiao, PhD Candidate in Ecology at Duke University Go inside the globe of the SECU Daily Planet Theater for live presentations and interactive shows led by scientists and educators. Meet researchers, witness live demonstrations, and engage in Q&A sessions with experts. With ever-changing topics and guests, there’s always something new and exciting to learn.
Source: NC Museum of Natural Sciences

item.title: Dueling Dinosaurs Sensory Friendly Mornings — Sun Aug 9, 10:00 AM — Downtown Raleigh
item.description:
Explore the Dueling Dinosaurs exhibit with reduced noise effects and smaller crowds. Please bring any noise-reducing headphones and fidgets you may need! A limited number of Sensory Friendly Bags are available for checkout at the front desk, and a limited number of noise-reducing headphones are available to borrow at the exhibit. Free registration is not necessary but encouraged; if you register, we’ll send reminder emails and resources about the exhibit so you can know before you go! Please note that this is a self-guided tour of the exhibit space (not led by a museum educator), though you may interact with the research team in the SECU DinoLab! Register Now!
Recommended Audience All ages, particularly neurodivergent audiences. Children must be accompanied by adults.
Questions? If you have any questions, please contact the Coordinator of Accessibility, Sam Frigerio, at Accessibility@NaturalSciences.org or 919.707.9824.
Source: NC Museum of Natural Sciences

item.title: National TRACK Trail Day — Sat Aug 15, 9:00 AM — Great Woodland Adventure Trail
item.description:
Join us for a family friendly trail workday to help take care of our beloved Great Woodland Adventure trail and keep it safe and beautiful for all TRACK Trail hikers.
Activities during this workday will include trimming vegetation, cleaning displays and statues, and other light trail maintenance. We plan to hike 0.4 miles around the loop trail to get to the worksite and will have to carry our own supplies out and back. No experience is required and all materials will be provided. item.title: OpenCourts Project - Biweekly Sync — Wed Aug 19, 7:30 PM
item.description:
Code with the Carolinas - Triangle Join volunteers at Code with the Carolinas for the biweekly meeting about OpenCourts, a project to build an open data portal for North and South Carolina legal data.. Starting with aggregate datasets from South Carolina courts, volunteers will be working to adopt this data (and our site being constructed to host it) to standards and measures more usable for accountability and analysis. These principles of analysis are drawn from guidance provided by the legal accountability organization [Measures for Justice](https://measuresforjustice.org/), whose limited work in the Carolinas we are trying to renew and expand.
This effort is building toward multi-state data portal that catalogues and publishes trusted, permissively-licensed court records to ensure open legal data remains a **public good** accessible to everyone. ️

item.title: Fun with Fungi Hike! — Sat Aug 22, 2:00 PM — Lake Shore Trailhead
item.description:
Join a Ranger at the Lake Shore Trailhead for a fun and engaging outdoor learning experience for all ages. Participants will explore and identify various mushrooms found within Lake Norman State Park and learn about their ecological importance. Plan to hike approximately 1.5 miles on varying elevation for the duration of the program.
**Please wear sturdy shoes that can get muddy and bring water. Consider bringing sunscreen, a hat, snacks, and a rain jacket (depending on weather). Restrooms and water are available further down Shortleaf Dr., closer to the picnic shelters. Note that Lake Shore Trail is a primitive, dirt trails that cannot accommodate wheelchairs or strollers.

item.title: CenterFest Arts Festival — Sat Sep 19 — Downtown Durham
item.description:
Since 1975, CenterFest has brought Durham together through art, music, food, and community. North Carolina’s longest-running outdoor juried arts festival returns to downtown Durham September 19–20, 2026, welcoming thousands of visitors to celebrate the creativity that makes Durham unique. This year’s festival highlights Durham Arts Council’s “Culture Lives Here” initiative as part of America’s 250th anniversary celebration. At the heart of the story is the DAC Building, originally built in 1906 as Durham High School and later serving as Durham City Hall. For generations, it has stood as a symbol of learning, civic engagement, and creativity. Join the Durham Arts Council on September 19–20 and take home a piece of Durham history with the commemorative design celebrating the creative spirit that continues to thrive in our city! Find out more information here.
Source: Resilient Durham NC

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Wed Oct 28 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

With this approach to qualitative inquiry, researchers can build on communication in daily life where diverse practices for sharing experience, making sense of experience, and imagining social change occur in personal narratives, sociocultural communications, and institutional policies.

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Wed Oct 28, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.description:
Speaker: Holli Saperstein, Executive Director, Wilmington Railroad Museum
Join us for a spooky edition of History at High Noon as we explore the mystery of the Maco Light, one of North Carolina’s most famous ghost stories! Reported for more than a century near old train tracks in Brunswick County, this legend tells the story of a ghostly railroad conductor named Joe Baldwin. After a tragic accident, believers have claimed to spot Baldwin’s spirit searching for his lost head. This talk will examine the real history behind the tale and how the story became an important part of local folklore, attracting visitors and curiosity from across the country!
For questions, please contact Stacey Smith at (919) 814-7032.

Data Science Raleigh As enterprises move from isolated AI assistants to interconnected agentic systems, orchestration is becoming a critical layer of the AI stack. Coordinating multiple agents across tools, data sources, models, and workflows introduces new opportunities for automation—but also new challenges around reliability, governance, observability, and control.
This session explores what it takes to design and operationalize agent orchestration in enterprise environments.
